ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, on a straight section of road, a school bus starts from rest at a traffic light and undergoes uniformly accelerated linear motion. After traveling $36\mathrm{m}$, its speed reaches $43.2\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$. It then maintains this speed and continues with uniform linear motion for $20\mathrm{s}$. Upon reaching the next intersection, the driver notices a red light ahead and immediately applies the brakes. The school bus undergoes uniformly decelerated linear motion and comes to a complete stop after traveling $36\mathrm{m}$ (take $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and the result can be expressed using radicals).

1. Find the magnitude of the acceleration $a_{1}$ for the uniformly accelerated motion of the school bus.
2. If the total mass of the school bus is $4500\mathrm{kg}$, find the magnitude of the resistance force when the school bus brakes.
3. If there is a student with a mass of $30\mathrm{kg}$ sitting in the school bus, find the magnitude of the force $F$ exerted by the seat on the student during the acceleration of the bus.

1. Find the magnitude of the acceleration $a_{1}$ for the uniformly accelerated motion of the school bus.
2. If the total mass of the school bus is $4500\mathrm{kg}$, find the magnitude of the resistance force when the school bus brakes.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a school bus on a straight road/intersection scene, with no numerical labels visible, so the quantitative data must come from the problem text. Then solve using constant-acceleration kinematic formulas. Convert the cruising speed: 43.2 km/h = 12 m/s. For the starting acceleration stage, use v^2-v0^2=2a1s with v0=0 and s=36 m to get a1. For braking, use 0^2-12^2=2as over 36 m to find the deceleration magnitude, then apply Newton's second law Fres=ma to the 4500 kg bus. For the student during acceleration, draw a free-body diagram: gravity mg downward, seat normal upward, and horizontal seat/friction force ma1 forward. The force exerted by the seat is the resultant of the vertical support mg and horizontal accelerating force ma1, so F=sqrt((mg)^2+(ma1)^2).

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, on a straight section of road, a school bus starts from rest at a traffic light and undergoes uniformly accelerated linear motion. After traveling $36\mathrm{m}$, its speed reaches $43.2\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$. It then maintains this speed and continues with uniform linear motion for $20\mathrm{s}$. Upon reaching the next intersection, the driver notices a red light ahead and immediately applies the brakes. The school bus undergoes uniformly decelerated linear motion and comes to a complete stop after traveling $36\mathrm{m}$ (take $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and the result can be expressed using radicals).

1. Find the magnitude of the acceleration $a_{1}$ for the uniformly accelerated motion of the school bus.
2. If the total mass of the school bus is $4500\mathrm{kg}$, find the magnitude of the resistance force when the school bus brakes.
3. If there is a student with a mass of $30\mathrm{kg}$ sitting in the school bus, find the magnitude of the force $F$ exerted by the seat on the student during the acceleration of the bus.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The attached figure shows a school bus driving on a straight road surface or near an intersection, and there are no numerical labels in the image that can be used for calculation; the required quantitative information comes from the problem statement text.

Reasoning: First convert the speed: 43.2 km/h = 43.2/3.6 = 12 m/s.
1. In the acceleration stage, it starts from rest, the displacement s = 36 m, and the final velocity v = 12 m/s. Using v^2 - v0^2 = 2a1s, obtain 12^2 - 0 = 2a1 × 36, so a1 = 144/72 = 2 m/s^2.
2. In the braking stage, the initial velocity is 12 m/s, the final velocity is 0, and the displacement is 36 m. Using 0^2 - 12^2 = 2as, obtain a = -2 m/s^2, so the magnitude of the deceleration is 2 m/s^2. The mass of the school bus is 4500 kg, and the magnitude of the resistance force F = ma = 4500 × 2 = 9000 N.
3. The mass of the student is 30 kg. During acceleration, the seat exerts on the student a vertically upward supporting force mg = 30 × 10 = 300 N, and also a horizontal forward force that accelerates the student ma1 = 30 × 2 = 60 N. The magnitude of the resultant force exerted by the seat on the student is F = sqrt(300^2 + 60^2) = sqrt(93600) = 60√26 N.
